title: Day 7 — Nothing To Flag
_comment: #39 (Phase 2). Second post-tutorial day, same footing as day 6 — no added_rules/removed_rules yet, no directive, rulebook still inherited from day_01.json with today's flips. archetype_mix is authored explicitly for the same reason as day 6: dark_web:1 has to be a declared slot, not a hope. Leans one more sneaky_bugger than day 6 and swaps in the_incompatible as this shift's quick-case breather, per the GDD's pacing note for that archetype.

rule_sheet.summary: Same rulebook as day six. Nothing on this sheet changed overnight — but read it again anyway, because more of today's applicants are built to survive a first read.
notes: A disposable email domain is still an automatic deny, no matter how clean the rest of the file looks.
Some of today's candidates will be spotless against every line on this sheet. Spotless is not the same question as fine — it just means the checklist ran out before the truth did.
A weak password behind weak encryption is still a flag, not a deny. Hygiene and malice are not the same file.
If nothing on the dossier, the sweep, the log, or the image gives you a reason, the rule is still: admit them.
